title: Selling his instrument to Red and giving up music
summary: Ridgley sold his horn to a traveling player called Red for $25 and never saw him again; the tape runs out.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Oh, when you quit, who did you give your music to? What did you give him?

Followed by the name of, we didn't know him nothing else but by Red. He didn't live here. He used to go, every year he'd come through on a cycle, see, like that. And we got to know him whenever he'd come, he'd always talk with us. So last time, before I stopped playing, he came through and I wanted to quit because I began to get pyreia, you know. And I asked him about taking my place in the band. And he said that he had to go to Tulsa, Oklahoma. That's where this band, the Psych is at. And he would write me when he got there and he did that. And so I wrote for him to come. He came in his home, it was kind of bad. And I let him use my own and he offered the bite and I sold it to him, see, for $25. I paid $192, I think that's $192 and a half, something like that for him. And I never did give him $5,000, I never did see him anymore. I haven't seen him since.
I'm afraid it's about to run out now.
Well, I think it's all right.
Yeah, so we'll just let it run on out. We still appreciate it.
He was back here in New Orleans. We never did, I never did see him anymore. So when I stopped playing music, I got rid of everything. I said, the gas and water didn't mix.
